events.description: Pope John XXIII convenes Vatican II, transforming Catholic worship (Mass in the vernacular), affirming religious liberty, and opening dialogue with Protestants and other faiths.
events.dateNotes: Vatican II, October 11, 1962 – December 8, 1965.

people.role: Pope who continued and closed the council

events.name: Lausanne Congress on World Evangelization
events.description: Billy Graham convenes about 2,700 evangelical leaders and guests from some 150 nations; the resulting Lausanne Covenant, drafted under John Stott, shapes evangelical mission for a generation.
events.dateNotes: July 16–25, 1974, Lausanne, Switzerland.

events.name: Christianity Shifts to the Global South
events.description: Between about 1980 and 2000 the center of gravity of world Christianity moved: the majority of Christians came to live in Africa, Asia and Latin America rather than in Europe and North America.
events.dateNotes: Estimates of when the crossover occurred vary with the counting method; see Philip Jenkins, The Next Christendom (2002), and Pew Research Center data.

events.name: Fall of the Soviet Union
events.description: The dissolution of the USSR on 26 December 1991 ends some seven decades of official state atheism and opens the former Soviet republics to far greater religious freedom, with a revival of Orthodox and other churches.
events.dateNotes: December 26, 1991.

locations.name: Eden
locations.description: Garden where God placed Adam and Eve (Gen 2:8-14). Its location is unknown: Genesis names four rivers, including the Tigris and Euphrates, and proposals range from southern Mesopotamia to Armenia; the world before the Flood may no longer exist. No coordinates are given.

locations.name: Ur
locations.description: Home city of Abraham's family, "Ur of the Chaldees" (Gen 11:28, 31; Acts 7:2-4), traditionally Tell el-Muqayyar in southern Iraq. Some scholars propose a northern Ur near Haran; the southern site is the majority identification.

locations.name: Haran
locations.description: Where Abraham's family settled before Canaan.

locations.name: Canaan
locations.description: The land west of the Jordan promised to Abraham (Gen 12:7; 17:8). The map pin marks the middle of the region, not a city.

locations.name: Egypt
locations.description: Where Israel settled under Joseph and was later enslaved. Scripture gives 430 years for the sojourn of Israel (Exod 12:40-41) and 400 years of affliction (Gen 15:13; Acts 7:6). On Ussher's chronology the 430 years run from Abraham's call in 1921 BC to the Exodus in 1491 BC, with about 215 years spent in Egypt (from 1706 BC). The pin is a centre-of-country marker.

locations.name: Mount Sinai
locations.description: Where God gave Moses the Law (Exod 19-20). Jebel Musa in the southern Sinai is the traditional identification (from about the 4th century AD); other proposals include Jebel Sin Bisher, Har Karkom and Jebel al-Lawz in Arabia (Midian). The site is not certain.

locations.name: Jerusalem
locations.description: City of David; location of the Temple.

locations.name: Bethlehem
locations.description: Birthplace of David and Jesus.

locations.name: Babylon
locations.description: Capital of Babylonian Empire; place of exile.

locations.name: Nazareth
locations.description: Hometown of Jesus.

locations.name: Capernaum
locations.description: Base of Jesus' Galilean ministry.

locations.name: Damascus
locations.description: Where Paul was converted.

locations.name: Antioch
locations.description: Center of early Gentile Christianity.

locations.name: Rome
locations.description: Capital of the Roman Empire; center of early church.

locations.name: Patmos
locations.description: Island where John wrote Revelation.

locations.name: Cana
locations.description: Galilean village where Jesus turned water into wine (John 2:1-11). Kafr Kanna is the traditional site; Khirbet Qana, about 13 km north of Nazareth, is a leading alternative.

locations.name: Sea of Galilee
locations.description: Lake where Jesus calmed the storm and walked on water.

locations.name: Bethsaida
locations.description: Fishing village on the north shore of the Sea of Galilee; home of Peter, Andrew and Philip (John 1:44). Et-Tell is the usual identification; el-Araj is a proposed alternative.

locations.name: Nain
locations.description: Village where Jesus raised the widow's son.

locations.name: Bethany
locations.description: Village near Jerusalem; home of Mary, Martha, and Lazarus.

locations.name: Gadara
locations.description: Decapolis city whose territory Matthew places the healing of the demon-possessed man in (Matt 8:28). Mark 5:1 and Luke 8:26 read "Gerasenes" (Gerasa or Kursi) in many manuscripts, and some read "Gergesenes"; the exact site is uncertain.

locations.name: Jericho
locations.description: Ancient city near the Jordan; site of Bartimaeus' healing.

locations.name: Tyre & Sidon
locations.description: Coastal cities of Phoenicia where Jesus healed the Syrophoenician woman's daughter (Matt 15:21-28). The map pin marks Tyre; Sidon lies about 35 km to the north.

locations.name: Decapolis
locations.description: League of ten Greco-Roman cities east of the Jordan.

locations.name: Jordan River
locations.description: River where Naaman was healed and Jesus was baptized.

locations.name: Samaria
locations.description: Philip preached and performed miracles here (Acts 8).

locations.name: Gaza Road
locations.description: Desert road from Jerusalem to Gaza where Philip baptized the Ethiopian official (Acts 8:26). The map pin marks Gaza at the end of the road.

locations.name: Joppa
locations.description: Where Peter raised Tabitha and had the vision of the sheet (Acts 9-10).

locations.name: Caesarea
locations.description: Roman capital of Judea; house of Cornelius; Paul's imprisonment (Acts 10, 23-26).

locations.name: Cyprus
locations.description: Home of Barnabas; first stop on Paul's first journey (Acts 13:4-12).

locations.name: Pisidian Antioch
locations.description: Paul preached in the synagogue; many believed (Acts 13:14-52).

locations.name: Iconium
locations.description: Paul and Barnabas preached but were driven out (Acts 14:1-7).

locations.name: Lystra
locations.description: Paul healed a lame man; later stoned (Acts 14:8-20).

locations.name: Derbe
locations.description: Lycaonian city where Paul and Barnabas made many disciples (Acts 14:20-21). Kerti Hoyuk is the usual identification; Devri Sehri is another proposal.

locations.name: Troas
locations.description: Paul received the Macedonian vision (Acts 16:8-10).

locations.name: Philippi
locations.description: First European church; Lydia converted; Paul imprisoned (Acts 16:11-40).

locations.name: Thessalonica
locations.description: Paul preached in synagogue; accused of sedition (Acts 17:1-9).

locations.name: Berea
locations.description: Bereans examined Scriptures daily to verify Paul's teaching (Acts 17:10-15).

locations.name: Athens
locations.description: Paul preached on the Areopagus about the Unknown God (Acts 17:16-34).

locations.name: Corinth
locations.description: Paul stayed 18 months; Gallio tribunal (Acts 18:1-17).

locations.name: Ephesus
locations.description: Paul taught 2 years; riot of Demetrius the silversmith (Acts 19).

locations.name: Miletus
locations.description: Paul's farewell to Ephesian elders (Acts 20:17-38).

locations.name: Crete
locations.description: Mediterranean island where Paul's ship put in at Fair Havens (Acts 27:7-12). The map pin marks the middle of the island.

locations.name: Malta
locations.description: Paul shipwrecked; healed the sick (Acts 27:39–28:10).

locations.name: Puteoli
locations.description: Port where Paul landed in Italy (Acts 28:13).

locations.name: Shechem
locations.description: Abraham built an altar here; Jacob bought land. First stop in Canaan.

locations.name: Hebron
locations.description: Abraham settled at the oaks of Mamre; burial site of the patriarchs.

locations.name: Beersheba
locations.description: Well of the oath between Abraham and Abimelech; Isaac and Jacob lived here.

locations.name: Goshen
locations.description: Region in eastern Egypt where Israel settled (Gen 45-47).

locations.name: Peniel
locations.description: Where Jacob wrestled with God and was renamed Israel (Gen 32:22-32).

locations.name: Red Sea Crossing
locations.description: Where Israel crossed the "sea" (Hebrew yam suph, "sea of reeds"; Exod 14). The exact place is unknown. Proposals include the head of the Gulf of Suez (the traditional area, shown here), the Bitter Lakes and Lake Timsah, Lake Sirbonis on the Mediterranean coast, and the Gulf of Aqaba.

locations.name: Marah
locations.description: Bitter waters made sweet by Moses (Exod 15:23-25). Ain Hawarah is the traditional identification and is uncertain.

locations.name: Elim
locations.description: Oasis with twelve springs and seventy palm trees (Exod 15:27). Wadi Gharandel is the traditional identification and is uncertain.

locations.name: Rephidim
locations.description: Where God gave water from the rock and Israel fought Amalek (Exod 17). Wadi Feiran is the traditional identification; other sites are proposed.

locations.name: Kadesh Barnea
locations.description: Israel camped before entering Canaan; spies sent out (Num 13-14).

locations.name: Nineveh
locations.description: Capital of Assyria where Jonah preached repentance.

locations.name: Emmaus
locations.description: Village about 60 stadia (c. 11 km) from Jerusalem where the risen Jesus appeared to two disciples (Luke 24:13-35). Its site is disputed: Emmaus-Nicopolis (Latrun, shown here) fits the reading of 160 stadia found in some manuscripts; Qubeibeh, Abu Ghosh and Motza better fit the 60 stadia of most manuscripts.

locations.name: Constantinople
locations.description: Capital of the Eastern Roman Empire; seat of ecumenical patriarchate.

locations.name: Carthage
locations.description: Important early church centre; home of Tertullian and Cyprian, and where Augustine studied and taught before his conversion.

locations.name: Hippo Regius
locations.description: Bishopric of Augustine of Hippo.

locations.name: Nicaea
locations.description: Site of the First Ecumenical Council (325 AD).

locations.name: Chalcedon
locations.description: Site of the Council of Chalcedon (451 AD).

locations.name: Wittenberg
locations.description: Where Martin Luther posted the 95 Theses (1517).

locations.name: Geneva
locations.description: Center of John Calvin's Reformed tradition.

locations.name: Mainz
locations.description: Gutenberg's city; birthplace of the printing press.

locations.name: Canterbury
locations.description: Seat of the Archbishop of Canterbury; English Christianity.

locations.name: Worms
locations.description: Diet of Worms (1521); Luther's "Here I stand."

locations.name: Trent
locations.description: Council of Trent (1545–1563); Catholic Counter-Reformation.

locations.name: Aldersgate
locations.description: Site of John Wesley's evangelical conversion (1738).

locations.name: Edinburgh
locations.description: Edinburgh Missionary Conference (1910).

locations.name: Azusa Street
locations.description: Azusa Street Revival (1906); birth of Pentecostalism.

locations.name: Serampore
locations.description: William Carey's mission base; Bible translation center.

locations.name: Qumran
locations.description: Site where the Dead Sea Scrolls were discovered (1947).

locations.name: Northampton
locations.description: Jonathan Edwards and the First Great Awakening.

locations.name: Assisi
locations.description: Home of Francis of Assisi.

locations.name: Nuremberg
locations.description: Center of Reformation-era publishing and reform.

locations.name: Whitby
locations.description: Synod of Whitby (664); Celtic vs. Roman church.

locations.name: Clermont
locations.description: Council of Clermont (1095); Pope Urban II calls the First Crusade.

locations.name: Wycliffe Country
locations.description: Home of John Wycliffe; Morning Star of the Reformation.

locations.name: Bethel
locations.description: Where Abraham built an altar and where Jacob dreamed of a ladder to heaven (Gen 12:8; 28:10-22). The identification with Beitin is widely accepted.

locations.name: Dothan
locations.description: Where Joseph found his brothers and was sold to the Ishmaelite traders (Gen 37:17-28); Elisha was later here (2 Kgs 6:13).

locations.name: Mount Ararat
locations.description: "The mountains of Ararat" (Gen 8:4) where the ark came to rest; the region is Urartu. Scripture names no single peak. Agri Dagi is the traditional modern identification; others propose Cudi Dagi.

locations.name: Mediterranean Sea
locations.description: The "great sea" west of Israel (Num 34:6); Jonah's ship sailed from Joppa toward Tarshish on it (Jonah 1:3-4). The pin is a point at sea off the coast.

locations.name: Gath-hepher
locations.description: Hometown of the prophet Jonah in Zebulun (2 Kgs 14:25; Josh 19:13). Identification with Khirbet ez-Zurra or Mashhad is probable.

locations.name: Mount of Olives
locations.description: Ridge east of Jerusalem: site of Jesus' Olivet discourse and of Gethsemane, and where the disciples returned from after the Ascension (Acts 1:12). Bethany lies on its eastern slope (Luke 24:50).

locations.name: Susa
locations.description: Winter capital of the Persian kings where Esther, Mordecai and Haman lived (Esth 1:2) and where Nehemiah served (Neh 1:1).

locations.name: Caesarea Philippi
locations.description: Where Peter confessed Jesus as the Christ (Matt 16:13-20). The Transfiguration followed about a week later on a "high mountain" that the Gospels do not name.

locations.name: Mount Carmel
locations.description: Where Elijah confronted the prophets of Baal (1 Kgs 18:19-40). Muhraka, at the south-east end of the ridge, is the traditional site.

locations.name: Smyrna
locations.description: City of the church addressed in Rev 2:8-11 and the see of Polycarp.

locations.name: Tel Aviv
locations.description: Where the State of Israel was proclaimed on 14 May 1948.

locations.name: Sodom
locations.description: One of the cities of the plain destroyed by God (Gen 18-19). Its site is disputed: Bab edh-Dhra at the south-east of the Dead Sea (pinned here) and Tall el-Hammam in the northern Jordan plain are the leading proposals.

locations.name: Alexandria
locations.description: Great Hellenistic city and early Christian centre: home of Apollos (Acts 18:24), Origen and Athanasius.

locations.name: Milan
locations.description: Imperial city where the Edict of Milan was issued (AD 313) and where Ambrose was bishop.

locations.name: Constance
locations.description: Site of the Council of Constance (1414-1418), where Jan Hus was condemned and burned (1415).

locations.name: Fair Havens
locations.description: Harbour on the south coast of Crete where Paul's ship put in and Paul advised against sailing on (Acts 27:8-12).

locations.name: Basel
locations.description: Rhine city and printing centre where the first edition of Calvin's Institutes was published in 1536.

locations.name: Mount Tabor
locations.description: Isolated mountain in lower Galilee, scene of Barak's muster (Judg 4:6). Since at least the fourth century it has been the traditional site of the Transfiguration; the Gospels name only "a high mountain" (Matt 17:1), and Mount Hermon is the main alternative.

locations.name: Mount Nebo
locations.description: Mountain east of the Jordan from which Moses viewed the promised land and where he died (Deut 34:1-5).

locations.name: Mount Gilboa
locations.description: Ridge on the south-east edge of the Jezreel valley where Saul and Jonathan died fighting the Philistines (1 Sam 31:1-6).

locations.name: Valley of Elah
locations.description: Valley between Socoh and Azekah in the Judean lowlands where Israel and the Philistines faced each other and David fought Goliath (1 Sam 17:1-3).

locations.name: Mizpah of Benjamin
locations.description: Town in Benjamin where Samuel gathered Israel to repent and judged them (1 Sam 7:5-6). The identification with Tell en-Nasbeh is widely accepted.

locations.name: Shiloh
locations.description: Site of the tabernacle and the sanctuary of Eli in the time of the judges (1 Sam 1-4).

locations.name: Aphek
locations.description: Philistine staging ground at the head of the Yarkon river, where Israel was defeated and the ark taken (1 Sam 4:1-11).

locations.name: Spring of Harod
locations.description: Spring at the foot of Mount Gilboa where Gideon tested his army before attacking Midian (Judg 7:1-7); the exact spring is a traditional identification.

locations.name: Gaza
locations.description: Philistine coastal city where Samson was imprisoned and died in the temple of Dagon (Judg 16:21-30).

locations.name: Mount of Beatitudes
locations.modernName: Mount of Beatitudes, near Tabgha, Israel
locations.description: Hillside above the north-west shore of the Sea of Galilee, the traditional site of the Sermon on the Mount; Matthew says only that Jesus went up "into a mountain" (Matt 5:1).

locations.name: Ein Karem
locations.description: Village in the hill country west of Jerusalem, the traditional home of Zechariah and Elizabeth; Luke names only "a city of Juda" (Luke 1:39). Location is by tradition.

locations.name: Lyon
locations.description: Roman Lugdunum; Irenaeus was bishop of its church in the second century.

locations.name: Nicomedia
locations.description: Eastern imperial capital under Diocletian; the first edict against Christians was posted there in February 303 and the church was demolished.

locations.name: Ravenna
locations.description: Residence of the last western emperors, where Odoacer deposed Romulus Augustulus in 476.

locations.name: Monte Cassino
locations.description: Hilltop monastery founded by Benedict of Nursia around 529, where the Rule is traditionally said to have been written.

locations.name: Mecca
locations.description: Birthplace of Muhammad and the first centre of Islam.

locations.name: Medina
locations.description: City of the Hijra in 622 and the base from which the early Muslim conquests began.

locations.name: London
locations.description: Capital of England; place of the Westminster Assembly, the King James Version commission and the founding of the British and Foreign Bible Society.

locations.name: Munster
locations.description: One of the two Westphalian cities where the 1648 peace treaties were negotiated and signed.

locations.name: Osnabruck
locations.description: The other Westphalian city where the 1648 peace treaties were negotiated and signed.

locations.name: New York
locations.description: Where the American Bible Society was founded in 1816.

locations.name: Barmen
locations.description: District of Wuppertal where the Confessing Church synod met in May 1934 and issued the Barmen Declaration.

locations.name: Vatican City
locations.description: Seat of the papacy; St Peter's Basilica hosted the Second Vatican Council.

locations.name: Lausanne
locations.description: Host city of the 1974 International Congress on World Evangelization.

locations.name: Moscow
locations.description: Capital of the Soviet Union, where the state was dissolved in December 1991.

locations.name: Vagharshapat
locations.description: Royal city of Armenia and, by tradition, the place where Gregory the Illuminator brought King Tiridates III to faith around 301.

locations.name: Axum
locations.description: Capital of the Aksumite kingdom, whose king Ezana accepted Christianity in the fourth century.

locations.name: Chang'an
locations.description: Tang imperial capital where the Persian monk Alopen was received in 635; the Xi'an stele (781) records the mission.

locations.name: Mikulcice
locations.description: Major stronghold of Great Moravia, the realm to which Cyril and Methodius were sent in 863.

journeys.name: Book of Acts
journeys.description: The spread of the early church from Jerusalem to Rome, following the narrative of Acts.

stops.label: Pentecost in Jerusalem
stops.description: The Holy Spirit descends on the apostles; Peter preaches and 3,000 are baptized.

stops.label: Stoning of Stephen
stops.description: Stephen is stoned; persecution scatters believers beyond Jerusalem.

stops.label: Philip Preaches in Samaria
stops.description: Philip performs miracles in Samaria; Simon the sorcerer believes.

stops.label: Ethiopian Eunuch Baptized
stops.description: Philip meets an Ethiopian official on the Gaza road and baptizes him.

stops.label: Conversion of Saul
stops.description: Saul encounters Christ on the Damascus road; Ananias restores his sight.

stops.label: Peter Raises Tabitha in Joppa
stops.description: Peter raises the disciple Tabitha (Dorcas) from the dead.

stops.label: Peter and Cornelius in Caesarea
stops.description: Peter receives a vision; the first Gentiles receive the Holy Spirit.

stops.label: Church Established in Antioch
stops.description: Believers first called "Christians" in Antioch; Barnabas and Saul teach.

stops.label: Barnabas and Saul in Cyprus
stops.description: Paul blinds the sorcerer Bar-Jesus; proconsul Sergius Paulus believes.

stops.label: Paul Preaches in Pisidian Antioch
stops.description: Paul's sermon in the synagogue; many believe but Jews stir up opposition.

stops.label: Iconium — Belief and Opposition
stops.description: Paul and Barnabas preach; the city divides; they flee before stoning.

stops.label: Lystra — Healing and Stoning
stops.description: Paul heals a lame man; mistaken for gods; then stoned and left for dead.

stops.label: Derbe — Many Disciples
stops.description: Paul and Barnabas make many disciples and begin the return journey.

stops.label: Council of Jerusalem
stops.description: Church leaders decide Gentiles need not be circumcised.

stops.label: Macedonian Vision at Troas
stops.description: Paul receives a vision: "Come over to Macedonia and help us."

stops.label: Lydia Converted in Philippi
stops.description: Lydia believes; Paul and Silas imprisoned; jailer converted.

stops.label: Paul in Thessalonica
stops.description: Paul reasons in the synagogue; accused of "turning the world upside down."

stops.label: Noble-Minded Bereans
stops.description: The Bereans examine the Scriptures daily to verify Paul's message.

stops.label: Paul on the Areopagus in Athens
stops.description: Paul preaches about the "Unknown God" on Mars Hill.

stops.label: Paul in Corinth — 18 Months
stops.description: Paul stays with Aquila and Priscilla; Gallio dismisses charges.

stops.label: Paul in Ephesus — 2 Years
stops.description: Extraordinary miracles; burning of occult scrolls; riot of Demetrius.

stops.label: Farewell to Ephesian Elders at Miletus
stops.description: Paul's emotional farewell: "I have not coveted anyone's silver or gold."

stops.label: Paul Arrested in Jerusalem
stops.description: Paul seized in the temple; transferred to Roman custody.

stops.label: Paul's Trial before Felix and Festus
stops.description: Paul held in Caesarea for two years; appeals to Caesar.

stops.label: Storm and Fair Havens of Crete
stops.description: Paul warns against sailing; a violent storm batters the ship 14 days.

stops.label: Shipwreck on Malta
stops.description: All 276 aboard survive; Paul bitten by a viper but unharmed; heals the sick.

stops.label: Landing at Puteoli
stops.description: Paul welcomed by believers at the Italian port.

stops.label: Paul Arrives in Rome
stops.description: Paul preaches the kingdom of God under house arrest for two years.

journeys.name: Book of Genesis
journeys.description: From Creation through the patriarchs — Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, and Joseph — ending with Israel in Egypt.

stops.label: Creation
stops.description: God creates the heavens, the earth, and mankind in His image.

stops.label: The Fall
stops.description: Adam and Eve disobey God and are expelled from the Garden of Eden.

stops.label: The Flood
stops.description: God judges the earth with a flood; Noah and his family are saved on the ark.

stops.label: Tower of Babel
stops.description: Humanity is scattered when God confuses their language at the tower.

stops.label: Call of Abraham
stops.description: God appears to Abram in Mesopotamia before he settles in Haran (Acts 7:2-4) and tells him to leave for a land He will show him (Gen 12:1-3). Ussher dates his departure from Haran to 1921 BC.

stops.label: Abraham in Haran
stops.description: Abram settles in Haran with Terah; after Terah's death, he departs for Canaan.

stops.label: Abraham at Shechem
stops.description: Abram arrives in Canaan; God promises the land. Abraham builds an altar.

stops.label: Abram in Egypt
stops.description: Famine drives Abram to Egypt; Pharaoh takes Sarai but is plagued.

stops.label: Abrahamic Covenant at Hebron
stops.description: God makes a covenant with Abraham at the oaks of Mamre, promising countless descendants.

stops.label: Covenant of Circumcision
stops.description: God establishes circumcision as the sign of His covenant with Abraham.

stops.label: Destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah
stops.description: Abraham intercedes; God destroys the cities but Lot escapes.

stops.label: Hagar and Ishmael at Beersheba
stops.description: Hagar and Ishmael sent away; God provides a well in the wilderness.

stops.label: Binding of Isaac on Mount Moriah
stops.description: Abraham's faith tested; God provides a ram as a substitute.

stops.label: Isaac Settles at Beersheba
stops.description: Driven by famine and strife from Gerar, Isaac settles at Beersheba, where God renews the covenant and Abimelech makes peace with him. Jacob and Esau had been born twenty years after his marriage (Gen 25:19-26).

stops.label: Jacob's Dream at Bethel
stops.description: Fleeing Esau, Jacob dreams of a ladder reaching to heaven and God renews to him the promise made to Abraham.

stops.label: Jacob Flees to Haran
stops.description: Jacob leaves home, reaches Haran and serves Laban for twenty years, marrying Leah and Rachel (Gen 29-31).

stops.label: Jacob Wrestles God at Peniel
stops.description: Jacob wrestles with God and is renamed Israel.

stops.label: Jacob Returns to Shechem
stops.description: Jacob returns to Canaan and buys land at Shechem; Dinah incident.

stops.label: Jacob Returns to Hebron
stops.description: Jacob comes to his father Isaac at Mamre (Hebron); Rachel has died near Bethlehem on the way (Gen 35:16-20). Isaac dies at 180 and is buried by his sons (Gen 35:28-29).

stops.label: Joseph Sold into Slavery
stops.description: Joseph's brothers sell him to traders headed for Egypt.

stops.label: Joseph Made Ruler of Egypt
stops.description: After interpreting Pharaoh's dreams, Joseph becomes second-in-command.

stops.label: Israel Enters Goshen
stops.description: Jacob's family (70 people) settles in Goshen at Pharaoh's invitation.

journeys.name: Book of Exodus
journeys.description: The deliverance of Israel from Egypt, through the wilderness to Mount Sinai and the building of the Tabernacle, then on to Kadesh Barnea and the Jordan.

stops.label: Israel Enslaved in Goshen
stops.description: A new Pharaoh arises who does not know Joseph; Israel is enslaved and multiplies.

stops.label: The Ten Plagues
stops.description: Moses confronts Pharaoh; God sends ten plagues upon Egypt, ending with the death of every firstborn.

stops.label: The Passover and Departure
stops.description: Israel keeps the first Passover and sets out from Rameses with great wealth.

stops.label: Crossing the Red Sea
stops.description: God parts the sea; Israel passes through on dry ground; Pharaoh's army is destroyed.

stops.label: Bitter Waters of Marah
stops.description: Israel's first crisis: bitter water is made sweet by a tree God shows Moses.

stops.label: Rest at Elim
stops.description: Israel camps at an oasis with twelve springs and seventy palm trees.

stops.label: Water from the Rock at Rephidim
stops.description: God provides water from a rock; Israel defeats Amalek while Moses' hands are raised.

stops.label: Giving of the Law at Sinai
stops.description: God descends on Mount Sinai in fire and thunder; gives the Ten Commandments and the Law.

stops.label: The Golden Calf
stops.description: While Moses is on the mountain, Aaron makes a golden calf; God's anger and Moses' intercession.

stops.label: The Tabernacle Completed
stops.description: Israel builds the Tabernacle according to God's pattern; the glory of the Lord fills it.

stops.label: Wilderness Wandering — Kadesh Barnea
stops.description: The twelve spies return; ten give a bad report. Israel is condemned to wander 40 years.

stops.label: Arrival at the Jordan
stops.description: After 40 years, the new generation reaches the Jordan River opposite the Promised Land.

journeys.name: Gospel of Luke
journeys.description: The life of Jesus from birth through resurrection, following Luke's orderly account.

stops.label: Zechariah in the Temple
stops.description: The angel Gabriel announces the birth of John the Baptist to the priest Zechariah.

stops.label: Annunciation in Nazareth
stops.description: Gabriel tells the virgin Mary she will bear the Son of God.

stops.label: Birth of Jesus in Bethlehem
stops.description: Jesus is born in a manger; angels announce the birth to shepherds.

stops.label: Presentation at the Temple
stops.description: Mary and Joseph present Jesus at the Temple; Simeon and Anna prophesy.

stops.label: The Boy Jesus in Nazareth
stops.description: Jesus grows up in Nazareth; at age 12 astounds the teachers in the Temple.

stops.label: Baptism of Jesus at the Jordan
stops.description: Jesus is baptized by John; the Holy Spirit descends; the Father speaks.

stops.label: Rejected at Nazareth
stops.description: Jesus reads Isaiah in the synagogue; his hometown tries to throw him off a cliff.

stops.label: Ministry Begins in Capernaum
stops.description: Jesus drives out a demon in the synagogue and heals Peter's mother-in-law.

stops.label: Great Catch of Fish
stops.description: Jesus calls Simon Peter, James, and John after a miraculous catch of fish.

stops.label: Raising the Widow's Son at Nain
stops.description: Jesus raises a widow's only son from the dead; "God has visited His people."

stops.label: Calming the Storm
stops.description: Jesus rebukes the wind and waves; the disciples ask, "Who is this?"

stops.label: Healing of the Gerasene Demoniac
stops.description: Jesus casts Legion out of a man among the tombs on the eastern shore; Matthew places it at Gadara, Mark and Luke at the country of the Gerasenes.

stops.label: Feeding of the 5,000 near Bethsaida
stops.description: Jesus feeds 5,000 men with five loaves and two fish.

stops.label: The Good Samaritan — Road to Jericho
stops.description: Jesus tells the parable of the Good Samaritan to a lawyer's question.

stops.label: Mary and Martha in Bethany
stops.description: Martha serves while Mary sits at Jesus' feet; "Mary has chosen the good portion."

stops.label: Healing of Blind Bartimaeus
stops.description: Jesus heals a blind man near Jericho; Zacchaeus believes.

stops.label: Crucifixion in Jerusalem
stops.description: Jesus is crucified at Golgotha; "Father, forgive them, for they know not what they do."

stops.label: The Empty Tomb
stops.description: Women find the tomb empty; angels declare, "He is not here; He has risen!"

stops.label: Road to Emmaus
stops.description: The risen Jesus walks with two disciples; revealed in the breaking of bread.

stops.label: Ascension near Jerusalem
stops.description: Jesus blesses the disciples and is taken up into heaven near Bethany.

journeys.name: Book of Jonah
journeys.description: The prophet Jonah flees from God, is swallowed by a great fish, and ultimately preaches repentance to Nineveh.

stops.label: God's Call to Jonah
stops.description: The word of the Lord comes to Jonah (the text names no place; his home was Gath-hepher): "Go to Nineveh, that great city, and cry out against it."

stops.label: Jonah Flees to Joppa
stops.description: Instead of obeying, Jonah goes down to Joppa and boards a ship bound for Tarshish — away from God.

stops.label: The Great Storm at Sea
stops.description: God hurls a great wind; the sailors cast lots; Jonah confesses and is thrown overboard.

stops.label: Swallowed by the Great Fish
stops.description: God appoints a great fish to swallow Jonah. He prays from its belly for three days and nights.

stops.label: Jonah Preaches in Nineveh
stops.description: Jonah walks through the great city crying, "Yet forty days, and Nineveh shall be overthrown!"

stops.label: Nineveh Repents
stops.description: The king and all the people repent in sackcloth and ashes; God relents from disaster.

stops.label: Jonah's Anger and the Vine
stops.description: Jonah is angry that God showed mercy. God teaches him compassion through a vine and a worm.
